newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INTERVIEW-Setron set to be tycoon's focus.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Setron set to be tycoon's focus.

text.p: Malaysian electronics manufacturer Setron (Malaysia) Bhd is set to become the main vehicle for the diverse and rapidly-expanding business empire of tycoon Amin Shah Omar Shah.

Setron, which currently makes and distributes Sanyo and GoldStar television sets in Malaysia, will eventually own 100 percent of the equity of unlisted Business Focus Sdn Bhd under a plan announced in May.
Asked by Reuters in an interview if investors could buy into Business Focus's success through shares of Setron, Amin Shah said this would be the case upon the restructuring.

Amin Shah is executive chairman of Business Focus, a privately-owned company that in turn controls and owns business interests as diverse as shipbuilding and property development to the manufacture of confectioneries.

The company, with 800 million ringgit ($320 million) in assets, has interests in Australia, South Africa, Italy and Peru. Amin Shah plans to expand to the United States and Britain, he told Reuters in the interview on Wednesday night.
The 42-year-old former political aspirant has just returned from a month-long fact-finding mission to the U.S.

"Initially our overseas ventures were only in countries like Albania, but now we can afford to be in places like Britain and the United States," said Amin Shah. "These countries are beneficial to us because of the ease of raising funds there."
When asked what exactly he plans on doing in the U.S. he said: "We will do in the U.S. what we are already doing now."

What Amin Shah has been doing is running some of his estimated 150 companies. In fact, his hands are so full that the businessman recently advertised for 50 chief executive officers to help him run his companies.
But the jewels in Business Focus's crown are the contract to build and service patrol vessels for the Royal Malaysian Navy and to develop the naval dockyard in the island state of Penang.

Penang Shipbuilding Corporation Bhd, which is the company holding the contracts, is a 51 percent-owned subsidiary of Business Focus. PSCI currently has orders worth around 100 million ringgit on its books.
Under the contract, PSCI will build and deliver 27 patrol vessels and fully service them for 15 years.
The road to success for Amin Shah has not been without its difficulties.

"Before I created Business Focus I was in debt, owing nearly 10 million ringgit," he said. But with help from close friends, he said he put together a string of deals involving the sale of aircraft to Malaysian Airline System Bhd's (MAS) Malaysia Airlines, which eventually pulled him out of debt.
"I created Business Focus in 1991 with just three million ringgit, and look where it is today," Amin Shah said.

Amin Shah had originally intended upon a career in politics. He was a member of the dominant United Malay National Organisation (UMNO) youth wing for more than 12 years, before his debts forced him to concentrate on his business ventures.

Stock analysts have traditionally shied away from covering any of the companies linked to Amin Shah. "Many of the stocks are just too speculative for us to really look at the fundamentals," said one local analyst.

One of the companies Amin Shah is set to turn around in coming years is biscuit maker Khong Guan Holdings (Malaysia) Bhd. Amin Shah, who owns 30 percent of Khong Guan, announced in September the acquisition of six new hotels in Malaysia, and one in China for a total of 384 million ringgit.
